messages:
maya: Heads up — seeing a recurring pattern of missing spans in the aggregator jobs over the past 6 days. Not just one-off drops; distribution shows gaps every ~90 minutes. Opening this thread to track remediation owners and timelines.

maya: Quick snapshot: the ETL consumer lag spikes coincide with a shard rebalance. Seems like the consumer checkpointing sometimes skips committing processed offsets when a rebalance happens.

eric: ugh. do we have an example trace id?

maya: example trace: 1a2b3c4d — missing spans between serviceA -> serviceB. I queried raw events: there are gaps in span ids for several requests.

sam: thanks — can you paste the consumer logs around a rebalance?

maya: pasted: ```
2026-03-20T07:12:01Z consumer-3 INFO Rebalance: losing partitions [5,6]
2026-03-20T07:12:01Z consumer-3 INFO processed offset 345678
2026-03-20T07:12:01Z consumer-3 ERROR commit failed: NotLeaderForPartition
2026-03-20T07:12:02Z consumer-4 INFO assigned partitions [5,6]
```

de*: commit failure looks like race during rebalance. we should retry commits on NotLeaderForPartition.

eric: agree. but commit retry alone might cause duplicates or reordering. need guard to ensure we don't ack before spans are fully persisted to object store.

devon: workflow note — the aggregator does two steps: 1) materialize spans into s3 (batch) 2) update aggregation index. If step 2 can run before step 1's commit is stable, downstream reads miss spans.

li: I can add a short-lived metric to detect "span-commit-latency" and a counter for "commit-error:NotLeaderForPartition". likely quick.

maya: action: add metric (li) and a detection alert for >50 errors/15m. owner: li. ETA: EOD today?

li: yep, will push metric and dashboard tile by EOD.

sam: action: add idempotent commit logic + bounded retries with backoff. owner: sam. ETA: PR by tomorrow lunchtime.

sam: propose adding a reconciliation job to detect missing spans and backfill them automatically for the last 24h. It could be a safe rollback remediation if aggregator misses them. owner: sam + devon. ETA: spike this week.

devon: I'll own the reconciliation job infra. Will coordinate with sam on the rehydrate logic.

maya: incident-bot: please create a ticket for the postmortem actions and a weekly follow-up.

incident-bot: Created ticket INFR-4321: "Recurring span loss during consumer rebalance". Assigned to @sam, @li, @devon.

eric: timeline question — do we want a hotfix first (quick retry logic) then infra (reconciliation), or the other way?

sam: hotfix first. can ship a retry with safe invariants fast. reconciliation is longer term.

maya: prioritize hotfix. Sam — do you need any support to validate on staging?

sam: yes — need access to the staging partition map + synthetic traces that reproduce the rebalance. @devon can you set that up?

devon: will provision a staging run with synthetic load and force rebalance. timeline: today afternoon.

li: also setting up the alert/metric; if we get alerts this week we can validate post-hotfix.

maya: accountability: list of action items —
- li: metric + alert (EOD today)
- sam: idempotent commit + retries PR (tomorrow lunchtime)
- devon: staging repro + reconciliation infra spike (this week)
- maya: write short postmortem note and link to runbook (EOD tomorrow)
- eric: review hotfix + approve rollout to dedicated cluster (tomorrow afternoon)

maya: please comment here when PRs/tickets are ready so we can track.

eric: I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow 11:30 to triage final rollout steps. Invite sent.

sam: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/inference/aggregator/pulls/1287 — contains retry wrapper and tests. please review.

maya: quick QA test plan: 1) force rebalance in staging 2) send synthetic traces 3) assert no missing spans for 10k requests 4) monitor commit-error metric.

devon: staging run done. I forced rebalance 3x and synthetic load started at 16:10 UTC.

li: alert fired once during the run (27 errors over 15m) before PR merge. After PR merge, re-ran tests and errors dropped to 0.

eric: sounds good. Maya — are we comfortable rolling this to prod tonight with a canary?

maya: yes. rollout plan: canary on 10% of traffic for 30m, watch commit-error and end-to-end span completeness metric, then 50% for 30m, then 100%. rollback on >5/min commit errors or any span completeness degradation.

sam: deploying canary now. will post updates.

incident-bot: Deploy started: aggregator-service v2.1.3-canary by @sam.

sam: canary 10% started — no alerts so far, 15m in.

li: dashboard looks clean. no missing-span counts in canary segment.

sam: canary to 50% — 10m in. all good.

sam: full rollout complete at 21:02 UTC.

maya: follow-ups: schedule weekly check of span completeness for 4 weeks. sam/devon to own the reconciliation job spike and add a daily backfill run if needed.

eric: add postmortem summary to INFR-4321 and link to dashboards/runbook.

maya: closing this thread for active work, will update INFR-4321 with owners and timelines. leave comments here if any regressions. :white_check_mark:
